earned_by: Disposable scoping probes on 2026-10-21, not evidence. With not-all-equal on every edge, square tori a x a with a odd gave E = 0.88, 0.82, 0.83, 0.86, 0.84 at a = 5, 9, 13, 17, 25, and a x 2a gave 1.10, 1.12, 1.13, 1.12, 1.17 (6,000 samples each). Honeycomb tori fell from 0.042 to 0 by 12 x 13; triangular tori rose from 3.6 to about 11 bits from 3 x 3 to 6 x 6. EMERGENCE-BITS-20261021-001B-P001 proves that bipartite networks hold 0, that a frustrating patch makes emergence grow with area, and that odd tori recolour into random implications plus seam clauses. The open question is size dependence.
question: Put a not-all-equal relation NAE(h_u, x_e, h_v) on every edge of a torus grid, with hidden joints h at the vertices and uniformly random visible spokes x on the edges. How does the emergence E = -log2 P[the spokes extend to the joints] depend on the size of the torus at fixed shape? Is it a size-independent positive amount on square-lattice tori with an odd side, while it vanishes on honeycomb tori with an odd side and grows with the area on triangular tori?

public_inputs.square_odd: a x a square-lattice torus, a in {9, 13, 17, 25, 33, 41} (both sides odd), 8,000 samples each
public_inputs.square_odd_by_even: a x 2a square-lattice torus, a in {9, 13, 17, 25, 33} (one odd side, shape 1:2), 8,000 samples each
public_inputs.honeycomb_odd: brick-wall honeycomb torus a x (a+1), a in {4, 8, 12, 16, 24} (odd rows of length a+1), 6,000 samples each
public_inputs.triangular: triangular-lattice torus a x a, a in {3, 4, 5}, 20,000 samples each
public_inputs.square_even_control: a x a square-lattice torus, a in {8, 16, 32} (bipartite), 2,000 samples each
public_inputs.parity_control: parity links on the 3 x 3 and 5 x 5 square tori, 500 samples each

definitions: Spokes are independent fair bits, one per edge. A sample is consistent when some assignment of the joints satisfies NAE on every edge; E = -log2 of the consistent fraction, with standard error by the delta method. Locally bipartite: the graph with the wrap-around edges of its odd sides removed is bipartite. Two solvers judge every square-torus sample: limited backtracking on the original relations, and strongly connected components on the recoloured form (tau = h xor ((i + j) mod 2): random implications on ordinary edges, monotone two-literal clauses on wrap-around edges joining equal colours), built directly from the spokes without the not-all-equal tables.
primary_observable: E per (family, size) with its standard error, and the least-squares slope of E against log2(a) for each square family

predictions.H_scale: For square_odd and for square_odd_by_even separately: the weighted least-squares slope of E against log2(a) has absolute value at most 0.04 bits per doubling, and every E exceeds 0.3 bits.
predictions.H_aspect: The mean E of square_odd_by_even exceeds the mean E of square_odd by at least 0.1 bits (secondary).
predictions.H_vanish: honeycomb_odd: E at a = 24 is below 0.01 bits, and the family's E never rises by more than 3 standard errors from one size to the next.
predictions.H_extensive: triangular: E rises strictly with a, and E per vertex at a = 5 is at least half of E per vertex at a = 3.
predictions.controls: square_even_control is consistent in every sample; the two solvers agree on every square-torus sample; on parity_control the solver agrees with the cycle-sum criterion on every sample; every square_odd and honeycomb torus is locally bipartite and not bipartite; triangular tori are not locally bipartite.

decision_rule: If any control fails, the run is invalid and no hypothesis is decided. Otherwise H_scale is supported when both square families meet its slope and floor conditions; refuted when either family's slope exceeds 0.04 in absolute value by more than three standard errors; inconclusive otherwise. H_vanish and H_extensive are decided by their stated conditions. The ticket is supported when H_scale is supported and H_vanish and H_extensive hold; refuted when H_scale is refuted; closed null otherwise. H_aspect is reported without affecting the verdict.
stop_rule: Stop immediately if a control fails; otherwise stop after the frozen roster.
seeds: random.Random(f'{family}-{a}-{b}') per row; the parity control uses random.Random('parity-{a}')
red_team_r0: Identifiability: E is a property of the declared torus and the uniform spoke measure; the estimate's only error is sampling, reported per row.
Leakage: no labels or expected values enter the producer; the predictions are evaluated only in result fields.
Solver error: every square-torus sample is judged by two independently written solvers on two independently built instances; any disagreement invalidates the run.
Finite size: sizes span a factor of 4.6 in side length; a slow drift below 0.04 bits per doubling would pass, so the nonclaims exclude any statement about the infinite limit.
Shape: the two square families differ in topology (two odd sides versus one) and are never pooled.
Multiplicity: one primary hypothesis decided on two families with a fixed threshold; the secondary hypothesis does not change the verdict.
nonclaims: Monte Carlo estimates on finite tori up to 41 x 41 and 33 x 66; no statement about the infinite limit and no proof of scale invariance.
The lattices are declared by the experimenter; this concerns emergence on given surfaces, not a constructed space.
Any link to critical percolation is an interpretation, not tested here.
forbidden_inputs: the expected verdicts or scoping values as inputs to the producer
any coordinate or metric in the consistency computation beyond the declared graph
